title: Coached practice: current intent and late responses

initial_facts.text: A user selects 'open' and quickly changes the filter to 'all'.
The list sometimes returns to the narrower result set.

public_evidence.text: F2 finishes first and renders all rows. F1 finishes later and overwrites the view.
Both responses are fresh network responses; no local cache is involved.
The view commits whichever response finishes last, without checking current filter intent.

coaching.lesson: A response may be valid for its original request and still be stale for the user's current intent.
guided_steps: Record the current query or filter.
Compare request start and completion order.
Check the rule that decides whether a response may update the view.
Test an older response arriving after a newer one.

accepted_alternatives: Use a monotonically increasing request generation guard.
Cancel obsolete requests and retain a current-intent guard for races.
Keep the current view while loading and announce the updated result accessibly.
